### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/runtime`, touching **10** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**3** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/api/error-handling-server.mdx`  _(via ScopedContext (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/automation/hook-bodies.mdx`  _(via ScopedContext (symbol, a top-level class), ScriptContext (symbol, a top-level interface))_
- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via ScopedContext (symbol, a top-level class))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `ObjectQL (symbol, 72 pages)`
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **53** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 21070a2f0ac944e930ab8c269e04d024d4a21eea` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `f59c7e5624b3f34f845666c21257cf9f3e9035eb` — the merge of head `0d133459d7af4eac7b5ea7dbbdefb44ab21c698c` into base `21070a2f0ac944e930ab8c269e04d024d4a21eea`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin f59c7e5624b3f34f845666c21257cf9f3e9035eb && git checkout f59c7e5624b3f34f845666c21257cf9f3e9035eb
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 21070a2f0ac944e930ab8c269e04d024d4a21eea 0d133459d7af4eac7b5ea7dbbdefb44ab21c698c && git checkout -B drift-repro 21070a2f0ac944e930ab8c269e04d024d4a21eea && git merge --no-ff 0d133459d7af4eac7b5ea7dbbdefb44ab21c698c

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 21070a2f0ac944e930ab8c269e04d024d4a21eea
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 21070a2f0ac944e930ab8c269e04d024d4a21eea` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `0d133459d7af4eac7b5ea7dbbdefb44ab21c698c`
Local-runs: none

Inputs: card #24197 (the body with its `Ruled:` line, and all 14 comments, among them claims 6248128513 and 6249052664, dispatch 6248210634, and the dev's `os-dev-report` 6248949940, which was read as claims to check); the PR #24274 record 6247399985, whose ③.6 is where this part comes from; PR #24307 (the body and the 13-file list); and the net diff `ef6564684342..0d133459d7` (+670 / −52). `ef6564684342` is the merge base of `origin/main` `30da04f8e0` and the head. The diff was read with `git diff` and `git show`. Nothing was built, run or re-run.

Check-runs on the head, read at 2026-10-18T11:15Z: 47 runs.
- 38 succeeded. Among them: Build Core, Build Docs, both Check Changeset runs, Governed Surface Queue Guard, every Lint job, the four Type Check jobs, TypeScript Type Check, Test Core 1/6, 2/6, 5/6 and 6/6, Spec property liveness, and the claim and card guards.
  - The first Check Changeset run started at 10:48Z, on the body before the re-declaration.
  - The second started at 11:05Z, after the body edit, and ran on the `Clause-②: yes (widening)` body.
- 7 were skipped by design: Console Pin Gate, the Dogfood shards, Dogfood Verify CLI, Temporal Conformance, Packed-tarball smoke, and the re-fired Auto Label and Check PR Size.
- 2 were still in progress and not waited on: Test Core (3/6) and Test Core (4/6). Those two shards are part of the gate verdict on the new pins. This record does not stand in for them, and the adopting seat reads their conclusions before the queue.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **`ObjectQL.serveFormulaField(objectName, record, field, context?)`** (`engine.ts`). NEEDED, and its contract is RIGHT.
   - **Mechanism.** It is the read path's own evaluation, call for call: `planFormulaProjection(schema, [field])`, then `applyFormulaPlan` with `resolveFormulaPermissions(…, this.permissionResolution(context))`, `formulaFaultSink(objectName)` and `resolveFormulaRelated(schema, plan, [scratch], context)`. These are the four calls `find` and `findOne` make (`engine.ts`, about lines 14018 and 14307). They run over a shallow copy, so the hook payload is never written.
   - **Inputs.** For a field that is not a declared formula, the plan is empty and the method returns `undefined`. That is the same "read the stored column instead" signal `resolveRecordTitle` already uses.
   - **Authority.** `resolveFormulaRelated` calls `resolveOneHopRelated(…, 'caller')`. Its hop query carries `context` unchanged; the `isSystem` spread belongs to the `'predicate'` arm only. The query goes through the public `this.find`, so every read layer applies.
   - **Transaction.** The hop reads with the channel's context, `transaction` included. Pinned: both hop driver calls carry the channel's handle.
   - **One hop.** `resolveFormulaRelated` is called without a query, so the record in hand serves its first hop. The hop query is then added to `formulaHopReads`, so the related object's own formulas serve no hop. Pinned: no `lib_shelf` read happens.
   - **Faults.** A related record that is missing or unreadable, and a second hop, leave the whole formula `null`, with the read's reason sent to the sink. There is never a partial string: `formulaHopScope` answers `ok: false` before anything is evaluated. A hop read that throws is caught as `unreadable`. A syntactically broken formula throws at `planFormulaProjection`'s compile, as `find` and the synchronous `evaluateFormulaField` already do.
   - **Why public.** `ScopedContext` reaches the method through the engine type, and a TypeScript `private` would refuse that call.
   - **One gap in the docblock, not the code.** The optional `context` is not described. An omitted context reads the way an engine `find` with no context reads. Only in-process code that already holds the engine can call this method, and it grants nothing `find` does not.

2. **`ScopedContext.serveFormulaField(objectName, record, field)`**. NEEDED and RIGHT.
   - It passes `this.executionContext`. That is the same object `ScopedContext.object(name)` hands to `ObjectRepository`, which passes it as `context` on every `find` and `findOne`.
   - `sudo()`, `withRunAs(…)`, `transaction(…)` and the begin trio each build a new `ScopedContext` over the same engine with the derived context, so the method follows every one of them.
   - It is the minimal route. The execution context is a private constructor field. A read through `object(…)` would rebuild the query object as `{ ...query, context }` and lose the identity-keyed `formulaHopReads` marker. This is the dev's deviation 3, and it is verified.
   - Every `new ScopedContext(` in non-test source is in `engine.ts`, over an `ObjectQL`, so the cast to `ObjectQL` holds at this head.

3. **`resolveServedRecordTitle(schema, record, channel)`, `servedRecordTitle(schema, row)` and the type `FormulaServingChannel`** (`record-title.ts`, exported from the `.` index). Each is NEEDED and RIGHT.
   - The runtime is the consumer, and it is a separate package. Both helpers reuse the module-private `toTitle`, so runtime holds no second normalisation of a title.
   - `resolveServedRecordTitle` keeps `resolveRecordTitle`'s shape: the formula leg first, the stored column when the pointer is not a formula, never the record's id.
   - For a formula pointer, `applyFormulaPlan` always writes the field (a value or `null`). So the stored-column fallback can never surface a stale stored value for a formula title.
   - `FormulaServingChannel` is a structural interface with one method. The body runner therefore tells a serving channel from `UnscopedHookApi` (`hook-run-as.ts`, which has no such method) with a `typeof` check, not by class.
   - `resolveRecordTitle` and `evaluateFormulaField` are unchanged apart from docblocks.

4. **The channel** (`body-runner.ts`, `buildTitleSurface`). RIGHT: no privilege escalation and no second connection.
   - The VM title wire resolves `txState.api ?? ctx.api` at call time and hands it in (`quickjs-runner.ts`, the title install).
   - `ctx.api` is `buildSandboxApi`'s seam Proxy over the hook's `ScopedContext`. The Proxy's default branch forwards `serveFormulaField` bound to that `ScopedContext`. `txState.api` is the ctx returned by the wrapped `beginTransaction`.
   - So the hop reads with exactly the identity, permissions and transaction the body's own `ctx.api.object(…).find` uses. It can wait on a connection only where that read would.
   - The VM cannot call `serveFormulaField` directly. Its `ctx.api` exposes `object(name)`, with four read verbs, six write verbs and the transaction leaves. The method is reached only through `ctx.title()`, with the hook's own object and that object's title pointer.
   - "The caller" means the channel's identity. For an inheriting hook it is the triggering caller. For `runAs: 'system'` (`sudo()`) it is SYSTEM, which is what that body's own reads already get.

5. **What `ctx.title()` answers now, case by case:**
   - **Own-column formula title:** computed over `hookRecordState` with 0 reads (pinned in both suites). It now also gets the `can()` map and whatever timezone the channel's context carries, as a read does. The synchronous path got neither. Not pinned.
   - **Title over lookups:** one batched read per reference field, through the in-flight foreign keys. That is the `beforeInsert` payload, a key moved in `beforeUpdate`, and the after-state in `afterUpdate` (all pinned). With the keys unchanged, it equals `findOne` for the same caller.
   - **Related record hidden or missing:** `null`, never the readable half and never the hidden name. `findOne` of the row answers `title: null` to the same caller (pinned H4, with the SYSTEM control). An empty reference is evaluated as on a read: the optional read gives its fallback, and a plain read faults to `null`.
   - **Second hop:** `null`, with no `lib_shelf` read, as on the read (pinned H5).
   - **Channel without `serveFormulaField`** (`UnscopedHookApi`, i.e. a `runAs: 'user'` hook with no user): the synchronous path. An own-column title resolves; a title over a reference answers `null`. This is exactly the base behaviour. No pin at this head reaches the branch, because every new and existing runtime pin runs on a `ScopedContext`.
   - **`ctx.title('field')`:** one `findOne` on the same channel, still gated on `api.read`. The title is read off the served row by `servedRecordTitle`, the related object's own one-hop title included (pinned H3, `Dune @ A-1`). If no row comes back, the answer is `null`.

6. **Parity with a REST read for the same caller.** RIGHT for the hop. Two exceptions predate this PR, which neither opens nor closes them:
   - (a) **Field-level security on this record's own title field.** The read masks it (`plugin-security` `field-masker.ts` deletes the key). `ctx.title()` does not, and it did not before for an own-column title either. The hop's related columns are themselves read under the caller's FLS, so nothing is composed beyond what the caller can read.
   - (b) The foreign-key column posture recorded in 6247399985 ③.8b.

   Parity is pinned against `engine.findOne` with the same context, not against the HTTP route (the PR body's Acceptance notes say no server was booted). The route serves `engine.findOne` plus the door's projection, so the two agree except for (a).

7. **The related-form change is a fail-closed tightening.** RIGHT. When FLS removes the related object's formula title from the served row, `ctx.title('field')` now answers `null`. Before, it re-derived the hidden value from the row's visible columns. Nothing that was accepted before is refused now.

8. **Gate-forced and doc rows.** RIGHT.
   - `quickjs-runner.ts`, `script-runner.ts` and `cli` `extract-hook-body.ts` change comments only.
   - `hook-bodies.mdx` now states the cost and the capability reasoning truthfully.
   - The two pins renamed in `hook-ctx-title.integration.test.ts` keep their assertions.
   - All of these rows are re-declared in claim 6249052664.

### ② Semver level

- **`@objectstack/objectql` `minor`: RIGHT.**
  - The `.` index gains two functions and one type. `ObjectQL` and `ScopedContext`, exported from both `.` and `./core`, each gain one public method. Nothing is removed, renamed or narrowed.
  - The changeset names the four functions and methods, and it describes their authority, their transaction and their null cases accurately. It does not name the type `FormulaServingChannel` (cosmetic).
- **`@objectstack/runtime` `patch`: RIGHT.**
  - No published shape moves; only the `ScriptContext.title` docblock changes. The accessor now does what its declaration already said.
  - The changeset leaves out the FLS consequence of ①.7 for the related form. That is worth one sentence, but it does not change the level.
- **`@objectstack/cli`:** no changeset is owed. One comment changes in `src/`, and nothing published changes.
- **`Clause-②: yes (widening)` on the PR body: RIGHT.**
  - `readClause2Line` reads it as declared, `yes`, arm `widening`: one key line, the arm parenthetical first, and the trailing reasoning ignored.
  - No narrowing arm is owed, because ①.7 refuses nothing.
  - The level axis's rule ("at least one moved package graded `minor` or above") holds through objectql. The Check Changeset run that re-fired on the edited body concluded success.
  - The claim's original `no` line (6248128513) became wrong once the index moved. Claim 6249052664 corrected it, as the dev's open question 4 asked.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. **Open question 1** (the related form reads the served value; A shipped). ANSWERED: A is right, see ①.7.
   - B doubles the hop cost for the same answer.
   - C would compute a title that FLS removed, because FLS deletes the key.
   - Every in-repo channel computes formulas on `findOne`. An embedder that did not would get `null`, which fails closed.
2. **Open question 2** (the bare form needs no capability; A shipped). ANSWERED: A is right.
   - The bare form's reads are bounded to the object's own declared title formula, one hop, on the body's channel (①.4). The body cannot point them anywhere else.
   - `hook-bodies.mdx` no longer says the bare form performs no read.
   - Consequence to record: a body with no `api.read` now learns the related columns its object's title composes. Those are exactly what any reader of the record sees in its title.
3. **Open question 3** (a channel without `serveFormulaField`; A shipped). ANSWERED: A is right, and it keeps the base behaviour unchanged (①.5). A pin on a `runAs: 'user'` hook with no user would stop that branch from going unguarded. Not blocking.
4. **Open question 4** (the Clause-② line). ANSWERED: `yes (widening)`. It is re-declared in 6249052664 and now on the body; see ②.
5. **Deviations.**
   - The export widening (②), the comment and doc rows (①.8) and the channel method (①.2) are all right, and all are re-declared.
   - The runtime's full suite ran on the pre-merge head `650581b9` only. The merge brought no objectql, runtime or cli source, and CI's Test Core shards are the verdict; two of them are still open.
   - The worktree, attribution and subscription notes are process, not contract.
6. **`out_of_scope_findings`** (the stored-metadata-body family, reached through a formula's one-hop read). NOT below the filing gate. It is a possible disclosure path that has not been measured, it has been on `main` since PR #24274, and it is ESCALATED for filing. It is not this PR's to fix: the fix belongs at the shared hop, and this PR adds no reach that a body's own read of the same object does not already have (see ③.2).
   - Filed as #24316. Under the family's security-card convention (#21207), this record names the category and the position only: `packages/objectql/src/engine.ts` `resolveOneHopRelated` (the caller-authority hop), the lint's one-hop admission, and the family's enumeration pin, which names no formula hop. The reviewer's detailed reading is withheld from GitHub and held by the adopting seat for the maintainer.

7. **The carried `adr_note_addendum`.** True of this head. The ADR-0079 note should add three things:
   - "the caller's permissions" means the body channel's identity, which is SYSTEM under `runAs: 'system'`;
   - a channel that cannot read (a `runAs: 'user'` hook with no user) answers `null` for a title over a reference;
   - field-level security on the title field itself is not applied to `ctx.title()` (①.6a).

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-24197-hook-title-one-hop`
Reviewed-by: `session_01JtSQQ3EWsbNPzyYMug1tXy`

**VERDICT: PASS**
